misreading: In Wrapped decoding, the NeedSymbol state (first byte after a separator) resets row_symbols to 0 and calls process_symbol without incrementing the counter, so every row after the first is allowed width+1 symbols. A valid 3+ row input (e.g. width 4, "QUJD\nREVG\nR0g=") is rejected with BadWrap at the second separator, and an over-long second row is accepted.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The only wrapped decode test has two rows with a short final row and EOF, so the miscounted second row never reaches a separator check.
prevention: When several code paths consume the same unit, make each update every counter; test repeated structures with at least three full repetitions, not just two.

misreading: The integer square-root binary search for edge_milli uses hi = 3_000_000_000, a bound for sqrt(d2) rather than sqrt(d2 * 1_000_000) (up to ~2.83e12). Any edge longer than 3,000,000 units is clamped to about 3e9 milli, corrupting edge_milli, perimeter_milli, longest_edge and hull perimeter at large coordinates.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests use only tiny coordinates (edges of 3-5 units), far below the clamping threshold.
prevention: Derive every numeric bound from the extreme allowed inputs after all scaling, and test arithmetic helpers at the maximum input range.

misreading: The two attempts fail differently, both where a trailing slash meets segment rules. F1 treats 'wildcard must be last' as 'nothing may follow it', rejecting a valid wildcard with a permitted trailing slash ("/files/*rest/") as InvalidPattern. F2 strips a final '/' as the trailing flag before splitting, so "//" and "/a//" are accepted (root/'a' with trailing slash) instead of failing at the empty segment (offset 1 / 3).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: No visible test uses a trailing-slash wildcard pattern or a doubled slash; the only trailing-slash case is a plain static route.
prevention: Test each element kind combined with every optional delimiter or suffix, including doubled delimiters, and turn every literal example in the spec into a test.

misreading: All four transpose implementations loop `for c in 0..cols { for r in 0..rows {..} }`, so a valid empty matrix like (0, usize::MAX) iterates ~1.8e19 empty outer iterations and hangs, despite the spec's warning not to iterate huge unused dimensions (F2-F4 additionally loop over huge row counts in mul when the output is empty; F3 also misplaces some syntax-error offsets and F4 overflows u128 on very long digit strings).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests only use tiny matrices; the empty case (1x0 times 0x2) has small dimensions, so no huge-dimension empty matrix is transposed.
prevention: When a dimension may be zero while another is huge, short-circuit empty results before looping; bound runtime by actual element count, not declared sizes.

misreading: All four files remove a final '/' as the trailing-slash flag before splitting segments, so the empty segment just before it goes unnoticed: F1-F3 accept "//" (as root with a trailing flag) and "/a//" instead of InvalidPattern/InvalidPath at 1 / 3, which the spec states explicitly. F4's version slices input[start..end] with start > end and panics on every trailing-slash pattern or path.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: No visible test uses any trailing slash or a doubled final slash; all patterns and paths are plain slash-free-ending routes.
prevention: Validate structure before stripping optional delimiters, and turn every concrete example given in the specification (e.g. '// fails at 1') into a test.
